epics.title: Phase 0: Foundation
epics.summary: Monorepo, documentation and CI so every later phase has a working base.

tasks.title: Monorepo with pnpm workspaces, TypeScript and Vitest
acceptance: pnpm install works from a clean clone
pnpm test and pnpm typecheck run across all packages

tasks.title: README, architecture and delivery plan
acceptance: README explains the idea and quick start
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md documents every OS concept as a concrete rule
docs/PLAN.md lists phases, sprints and tasks

tasks.title: CI workflow: install, typecheck, test
acceptance: GitHub Actions runs on push and pull requests

epics.title: Phase 1: Kernel
epics.summary: @eatos/core: event-sourced state and a scheduler with priority classes, interrupts, re-prioritisation, inversion handling, health checks and a safety floor.

tasks.title: Domain types: priorities, tasks, events, profile, members, foods, pantry
acceptance: P0–P3 priority classes
Discriminated union of events

tasks.title: Event log and state reducer
acceptance: replay(events) equals step-by-step reduce
Safe mode derived from illness events

tasks.title: Daily routine scheduler
acceptance: Meals, medication (P0, 30 min deadline), hydration checkpoints and wind down

tasks.title: Interrupt handlers: calendar, workout, sleep, illness (safe mode)
acceptance: Meeting moves overlapping meal with a reason
Long workout adds recovery snack and raises targets
Safe mode: no snack, gentle meals, fluids P0

tasks.title: Re-prioritisation (EDF) and priority inversion
acceptance: Due tasks ordered by priority then deadline
Snack before a meal inherits priority and is kept light
Snack within 45 min is folded in

tasks.title: Health checks and safety floor
acceptance: Hydration, protein and fibre vs time-of-day curve
Energy floor goes critical when very little is eaten
Goals pause in safe mode

epics.title: Phase 2: Intelligence
epics.summary: Which food serves a need, for whom, with reasons.

tasks.title: Seed food catalog with nutrients, tags, allergens and safe variants
acceptance: 30+ foods across all slots
Nut-free and peanut-free variants linked with variantOf

tasks.title: Recommender with hard filters, soft scoring and reasons
acceptance: Never breaks an allergy or diet
Prefers expiring pantry items and says so
Respects time limits and exclusions

tasks.title: Preference memory with decay
acceptance: 60-day half-life
"Never" is hard for a year, a later "liked" lifts it

tasks.title: Housekeeping: pantry expiry, use-soon, compaction
acceptance: Expired items removed via events
Compaction keeps profile, feedback, pantry and safe mode

tasks.title: Household fit matrix and conflict resolution
acceptance: Fit per member with reason
Conflicting request swapped for a safe variant

tasks.title: Ask EatOS rule-based parser
acceptance: Understands minutes, mood, slot, need, exclusions and who is eating
No network or paid model

tasks.title: Day simulator CLI
acceptance: pnpm simulate prints schedule, checks, suggestions and the change log

tasks.title: Weekly plan and grocery list
acceptance: Every slot planned for 7 days
Batch cooking: dinner returns as next-day lunch
Grocery list excludes what is in the pantry

epics.title: Phase 3: API
epics.summary: HTTP server exposing the kernel so web, mobile and third parties share one backend.

tasks.title: HTTP syscalls
acceptance: /v1/events, /v1/now, /v1/schedule, /v1/health, /v1/recommend, /v1/ask, /v1/pantry, /v1/week, /v1/log, /v1/state

tasks.title: Per-user event log persistence
acceptance: One JSON file per user
Restart rebuilds state from the log

tasks.title: API tests
acceptance: Vitest covers each route, validation and persistence

epics.title: Phase 4: App shell, mobile and web
epics.summary: One Expo app for iOS, Android and web built from the design canvas, kernel on the device.

tasks.title: Expo app with kernel on the device
acceptance: Expo Router app builds for web
Uses @eatos/core directly

tasks.title: Theme tokens, light and dark
acceptance: Colours from the design
Follows system setting, with a Light/Dark/System choice

tasks.title: Onboarding: who's eating, diet, allergies
acceptance: Creates the profile event

tasks.title: Now and Ask screens
acceptance: Next up card with reasons, health tiles, plan-adjusted notice, coming up
Ask returns 3 options, Choose for me, Why these

tasks.title: Plan, Grocery and Pantry screens
acceptance: Weekly plan with batch cooking
Grocery list with checkboxes
Pantry with use-soon and add item

tasks.title: Cooking, Household and Profile screens
acceptance: Cooking steps and pantry status
Household fit and conflict resolution
Settings, safety floor, export

tasks.title: Responsive web layout
acceptance: Wide screens show a two-column dashboard
Works at phone width

tasks.title: Local persistence of the event log
acceptance: Event log saved on the device and restored on launch

epics.title: Phase 5: Sync and integrations
epics.summary: Connect EatOS to the world around the person so they log less.

tasks.title: Device to server sync of event logs
acceptance: Append-only merge by event id
Server cursor and epoch; devices resync fully after compaction
Works offline and reconciles
Off by default; turned on per device with a sync code

tasks.title: Calendar driver
acceptance: Reads iCalendar (.ics) files: UTC, TZID with daylight saving, folding, DURATION
Expands daily and weekly recurring events with INTERVAL, COUNT, UNTIL, BYDAY and EXDATE
Free/busy only: titles are dropped unless the person opts in
Stable event ids so importing twice adds nothing

tasks.title: Health data and wearable drivers
acceptance: Reads Apple Health export.xml: workouts, sleep nights, dietary water
Reads a simple CSV (type,start,end,value)
Workouts raise targets, short sleep moves the wind down
Stable ids so re-importing adds nothing

tasks.title: Grocery and delivery drivers
acceptance: Receipts become pantry items with quantities, places and use-by dates
Delivery menus are ranked for everyone eating; missing allergen or diet info is treated as unsafe
Ordered dishes can be logged as intake

tasks.title: Optional LLM adapter for Ask EatOS
acceptance: Same ParsedAsk shape as the rule parser
Off by default; the person supplies their own key and model
Only the typed sentence is sent: no profile, allergies, pantry or health data
Model output is validated strictly; any error, refusal, timeout or bad JSON falls back to the on-device parser
Allergies and diets are enforced by the recommender, never by the model

epics.title: Phase 6: Hardening and release
epics.summary: Make EatOS safe, private and ready to ship.

tasks.title: Encryption at rest, export and delete
acceptance: Event log and saved secrets encrypted on device with a passphrase; app starts locked
Wrong passphrase and tampering are rejected
Encrypted backups and restore, plain or encrypted
Server files encrypted at rest with EATOS_DATA_KEY
One-step export, and delete that also removes the server copy

tasks.title: Accessibility audit
acceptance: axe-core (WCAG 2.0 to 2.2, A and AA) finds no violations on every screen, light and dark, phone and desktop
Every control is at least 44 x 44 px
Keyboard focus is visible
Switches, checkboxes and progress bars are labelled for screen readers

tasks.title: End-to-end tests
acceptance: Playwright drives the built web app: onboarding, every screen, cooking to eaten, sync between two browsers, encryption and unlock, backups and restore, imports, optional Claude Ask (stubbed)
pnpm e2e runs the build, the journey and the accessibility audit
CI runs it on every push and uploads screenshots

tasks.title: Release pipeline: app config, icons, EAS, Pages, Docker, release guide
acceptance: App config with bundle ids, generated icons and splash, EAS build profiles
Web build deploys to GitHub Pages and works under a sub-path
A tagged release re-runs every check and attaches the web build
API ships as a Docker image with encrypted storage required
docs/RELEASE.md lists every step, including the ones only the account owner can do

tasks.title: Publish to the app stores and turn on Pages (owner action)
acceptance: Repository: Settings > Pages > Source: GitHub Actions
Expo account, eas init, and the EXPO_TOKEN secret
Apple Developer and Google Play accounts, signing credentials, store listings and privacy policy
Answer Apple's export-compliance and Google's data-safety questionnaires
First production build submitted with eas submit
